slides.label: KEY IDEA 01
slides.title: CPU Pipeline
slides.body: A modern CPU pipeline has 5+ stages: Fetch, Decode, Execute, Memory, Writeback. Each stage takes one or more clock cycles. Hazards stall the pipeline.

slides.label: KEY IDEA 02
slides.title: Branch Prediction
slides.body: The penalty for a mispredicted branch is 10-20 cycles (the pipeline depth). Modern predictors achieve 95%+ accuracy. Bimodal predictors use a 2-bit saturating counter per branch. GShare predictors use a global history register XORed with the branch address.

slides.label: KEY IDEA 03
slides.title: Cache Hierarchy
slides.body: CPUs have 2-3 levels of cache. L1 is 32KB per core, 4-cycle latency. L2 is 256-512KB per core, 12-cycle latency. L3 is 8-64MB shared, 40-cycle latency. Main memory is 100+ cycle latency.

slides.label: KEY IDEA 04
slides.title: NUMA
slides.body: Non-Uniform Memory Access means each processor socket has its own memory controller. Accessing local memory is 1-2x faster than remote. Linux exposes NUMA topology via sysfs. The numactl tool binds processes to specific nodes.
